hero.lead: An island of 21.8 million that restructured its debts, has drawn $2.4 billion under its IMF programme since 2023, and keeps nine in ten of its children in school.

stats.label: Drawn under the IMF programme since 2023

capital.heading: Sri Lanka has rebuilt its credit after default. Next, a clean stove in every home.

record.text: Total public debt (gross) at end-June 2026, provisional: LKR 32,977 billion (USD 97,952 million); total debt of the government LKR 31,999 billion
Extended Fund Facility, approved 20 March 2023: about $2.4 billion drawn; about $695 million made available in May 2026
International sovereign bonds, face amount at end-2023: 98% exchanged in the restructuring settled on 20 December 2024; upfront debt stock reduction of USD 3.0 billion
Rapid Financing Instrument, approved 19 December 2025: emergency support after Cyclone Ditwah
Post-Cyclone Ditwah Reconstruction and Livelihood Support Project: roads, irrigation, and the livelihoods and housing of cyclone-affected households; loan agreements signed 18 August 2026

register.name: International sovereign bond exchange
register.detail: Settlement concluded 20 December 2024 · 96% participation · 98% of the bonds exchanged
register.note: Face amount of the international sovereign bonds at end-2023
register.text: Sri Lanka exchanged its existing international sovereign bonds for new restructured bonds, on terms that introduced Macro-Linked Bonds. The Ministry of Finance puts the upfront reduction in debt stock at USD 3.0 billion, which can rise to USD 4.3 billion in an economic downturn, and the cut in debt service during the four-year IMF programme at USD 9.6 billion.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility, seventh review
register.detail: Staff-level agreement 4 October 2026 · SDR 254 million · Subject to IMF Executive Board approval
register.note: Board approval depends on the 2027 Budget and a financing assurances review
register.text: On Board approval Sri Lanka would draw about US$345 million, bringing disbursements under the arrangement to about US$2.7 billion. Approval depends on the Minister of Finance presenting to Parliament a 2027 Budget in line with programme parameters, and on a financing assurances review of multilateral partners’ contributions. Staff also urged faster recovery and reconstruction after Cyclone Ditwah.

register.name: Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project, new financing
register.detail: Approved 30 September 2026 · IDA Crisis Response Window · Extends the project by three years
register.note: 600 km of roads severely damaged by Cyclone Ditwah
register.text: Repairs and rebuilds 600 kilometres of roads severely damaged by Cyclone Ditwah, with priority for roads that restore access to markets, schools and health facilities. The World Bank expects it to benefit more than 830,000 people directly and to reach close to two million across eight target districts, which serves the livelihood, education and health standards.

register.name: Reforms for Growth, Resilience and Openness Development Policy Operation (REGROW DPO)
register.detail: Approved 29 June 2026 · Announced 1 July 2026 · Development policy operation · Budget support
register.note: Trade, investment climate, financial sector, state enterprise and power sector reforms
register.text: Budget support for reforms that reduce trade barriers, improve the investment climate and strengthen the financial sector, with measures to expand women’s employment, improve the governance of state-owned enterprises and make the power sector more competitive. Lower energy costs and more jobs serve the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility
register.detail: Approved 20 March 2023 · SDR 2.286 billion, 395 percent of quota · Combined fifth and sixth reviews completed 27 May 2026
register.note: About $2.4 billion drawn; about $695 million made available in May 2026
register.text: The IMF arrangement approved on 20 March 2023, worth SDR 2.286 billion (about US$3 billion). Completion of the combined fifth and sixth reviews gave immediate access to SDR 508 million (about US$695 million), bringing purchases under the arrangement to SDR 1.778 billion (about US$2.4 billion).

register.name: Rapid Financing Instrument
register.detail: Approved 19 December 2025 · SDR 150.5 million · 26 percent of quota
register.note: Urgent balance-of-payments and fiscal pressures after Cyclone Ditwah
register.text: An IMF disbursement of about US$206 million to help address urgent balance-of-payments and fiscal pressures arising from Cyclone Ditwah. The fifth review of the Extended Fund Facility was deferred at the time.

register.name: Sri Lanka Digital Transformation Project
register.detail: Approved 19 December 2025 · Online citizen service portal, data exchange and digital skills
register.note: Government services online and support for technology start-ups
register.text: Builds an integrated online portal for government services, with cross-agency data exchange and a cloud platform, and trains citizens and public servants to use them. It also funds a digital start-up accelerator, including for women entrepreneurs, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Secure, Affordable, and Sustainable Energy for Sri Lanka
register.detail: Approved 20 June 2025 · Includes $40 million in World Bank Group guarantees in the first phase
register.note: 1 gigawatt of new solar and wind; more than $800 million of private investment expected
register.text: A World Bank Group programme to add 1 gigawatt of clean electricity to the grid through new solar and wind projects and to mobilise more than $800 million in private investment. It supports Sri Lanka’s goal of generating 70 percent of its electricity from renewable sources by 2030, and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Loan to advance digital transformation
register.detail: Approval announced 10 November 2026
register.note: To advance digital transformation in Sri Lanka
register.text: An Asian Development Bank loan of $98 million to advance digital transformation in Sri Lanka, announced on 10 November 2026.

register.name: Financing to ensure safe and resilient water services
register.detail: Approval announced 9 November 2026 · Two projects
register.note: To expand and strengthen water supply and sanitation services across Sri Lanka
register.text: The Asian Development Bank has approved two projects, together $300 million, to expand and strengthen water supply and sanitation services across Sri Lanka, announced on 9 November 2026. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Promoting Resilience and Opportunity for Inclusive Recovery Sector Development Program
register.detail: Approved 21 October 2026 · $50 million policy-based loan · $50 million project loan
register.note: 30,000 households from the Aswesuma social registry, in six districts
register.text: Supports reforms and investments in social protection, economic inclusion and resilience for poor and elderly Sri Lankans, through the government’s National Empowerment Program. Households receive livelihood grants, employment and business support, skills development and financial literacy training, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Skills Development System Transformation Program
register.detail: Approved 29 September 2026 · Results-based loan · $50 million regular and $50 million concessional · $500,000 technical assistance grant
register.note: More than 100,000 young people expected to benefit
register.text: A results-based loan to improve the quality and relevance of technical and vocational training, link training providers with industry and widen job opportunities for young people, including nontraditional jobs for women in automotive technology and renewable energy. It serves the education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Trade, Investment and Industry Development Program, Subprogram 1
register.detail: Signed 18 August 2026 · Policy-based loan · Raised from $100 million to $200 million
register.note: General budgetary assistance; Subprogram 2, an indicative $100 million, expected to be implemented in 2028
register.text: A policy-based loan from the Asian Development Bank that gives general budgetary assistance, signed at the General Treasury in Colombo. The Ministry of Finance says it comes amid heightened economic uncertainty from the Middle East crisis and climate-related shocks, and that the loan was raised from USD 100 million to USD 200 million. Support for trade and investment serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Post-Cyclone Ditwah Reconstruction and Livelihood Support Project
register.detail: Loan agreements signed 18 August 2026 · Implementation 2026 to 2030
register.note: Roads, irrigation, and the livelihoods and housing of cyclone-affected households
register.text: Rehabilitates and rebuilds road infrastructure and irrigation systems damaged by Cyclone Ditwah, and restores the livelihoods and housing of cyclone-affected households. It serves the shelter, food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Rooftop Solar Aggregation and Virtual Net Metering Project
register.detail: Approved 26 June 2026 · $35 million concessional loan · $16.9 million EU grant · $5.5 million grant from the Japan Fund for the Joint Crediting Mechanism · Total cost $80.5 million
register.note: About 25 megawatt-peak of rooftop solar
register.text: About 25 megawatt-peak of rooftop solar, whose power the two electricity distribution utilities pool and share as credits with eligible small businesses and community organisations, including those unable to install rooftop solar because of financial or space constraints. It serves the energy standard.
by: Japan Fund for the Joint Crediting Mechanism

register.name: Kerawalapitiya–Port L Second Transmission Line Project
register.detail: Signed 8 October 2025 · Sovereign-backed financing · Second underground 220 kV cable into Colombo
register.note: Carries renewable power from the north and east to Colombo
register.text: Adds a second underground 220 kV cable between Kerawalapitiya and the Colombo Port L substation, to keep power supply uninterrupted and the grid stable. It helps move renewable power from the north and east to Colombo, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: Project for the Improvement of the Pump Station in Kelani River Basin
register.detail: Grant agreement signed 28 October 2026 · Gampaha District, Western Province
register.note: A drainage pumping station to reduce flood damage, in Gampaha District
register.text: A Japanese grant for a drainage pumping station and consulting services in the Kelani River Basin, to reduce flood damage by improving stormwater drainage capacity. Fewer floods protect homes, which serves the shelter standard.

register.name: New Anthoney’s Farms, poultry expansion
register.detail: Approved 10 October 2025 · Signed 2 June 2026 · Invested 29 October 2026 · C Loan from IFC and GAFSP, with an option to convert into equity
register.note: IFC loan of $5 million; up to $5 million expected from the GAFSP Private Sector Window
register.text: A loan from IFC and the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program to a Sri Lankan poultry business established in 1986, with a feed mill, breeder farms, a hatchery, broiler and out-grower farms, processing and its own retail shops. It part-funds a programme to expand capacity, improve efficiency and grow the retail network, which serves the food and livelihood standards.
by: Global Agriculture and Food Security Program

register.name: WindForce PLC, 100 MW solar plant
register.detail: Approved 3 April 2026 · Signed 27 April 2026 · Invested 15 September 2026 · Loan in Sri Lankan rupees, up to $18 million equivalent
register.note: A 100 MW ground-mounted solar plant in the Siyabalanduwa area, Uva Province
register.text: An IFC local-currency loan to WindForce PLC, which IFC describes as Sri Lanka’s largest renewable energy company, for its equity in a 100 MW ground-mounted solar photovoltaic project. It is supported by the IDA21 Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Nations Trust Bank, SME loan
register.detail: Approved 11 December 2025 · Signed 19 December 2025 · Invested 16 January 2026 · Four-year senior unsecured loan · Package of up to $70 million with a $20 million trade facility
register.note: On-lending to small and medium-sized enterprises, including women-owned SMEs
register.text: An IFC loan to Nations Trust Bank, a publicly listed licensed commercial bank, for on-lending to small and medium-sized enterprises, including women-owned SMEs, which face significant financing gaps. It serves the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 20 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy street in Colombo, Sri Lanka

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Green tea plantations on misty hills in central Sri Lanka

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Tropical rainforest in Sinharaja Forest Reserve, Sri Lanka

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: A reservoir and paddy fields in the dry zone of Sri Lanka

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of electricity from renewables, 2023
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: Wind turbines on the coast of Mannar, Sri Lanka

items.name: New Anthony’s Farm Group (NAF)
items.text: One of Sri Lanka’s leading fully integrated poultry producers, founded in 1986, working from breeding and feed to processing, distribution, exports and retail. In June 2026 IFC announced it will invest up to $10 million, including up to $5 million from the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program, to scale capacity; the project is expected to benefit at least 200 smallholder farmers.

items.name: WindForce PLC
items.text: Develops, owns and operates wind, solar and small hydropower assets; IFC describes it as Sri Lanka’s largest independent renewable energy producer. In April 2026 IFC announced it is investing up to $18 million through a local-currency loan for a utility-scale 100-megawatt solar power facility.

items.name: Sunshine Healthcare Lanka
items.text: A pharmaceutical and medical products business wholly owned by Sunshine Holdings PLC, with a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility, six regional distribution centres and access to over 3,000 pharmacies. IFC made an equity investment, approved in April 2024, for the expansion of pharmaceutical manufacturing, distribution and retail.

items.name: Nations Trust Bank
items.text: A publicly listed licensed commercial bank in Sri Lanka, established in 1999. IFC’s loan of up to $50 million, invested in January 2026, is for on-lending to small and medium-sized enterprises, including women-owned SMEs.
